value: This article provides a comprehensive overview of fiber bundles, fundamental topological structures defined by their local triviality and a consistent "typical fiber." It details various essential types, including principal bundles, which feature a structure group acting on the fiber, and vector bundles, crucial in geometry and physics. The discussion extends to their generalizations in higher category theory and noncommutative geometry, illustrating their wide applicability. Furthermore, the article extensively catalogues related concepts such as characteristic classes and various cohomology theories, which are indispensable tools for classifying and studying the properties of bundles.
